## 5. Lifetime measurement

Because no real frame owner exists, a synthetic frame loop was **not** treated
as production evidence.

A diagnostic harness nevertheless used the actual production classes:

```text
Component
   ↓
RuntimeGraph
   ↓
resolve_component()
   ↓
ResolutionCache
```

### 32 components / 60 diagnostic frame boundaries

```text
first boundary misses       32
subsequent hits           1888
final entries               32
```

The graph was rebuilt at each boundary. Identical resolution fingerprints
reused the immutable cached results.

This proves cache capability across rebuilt graph objects. It does **not** prove
that the application currently has a frame loop owning such a cache.

---

## 6. Real scene-adjacent cardinality

The existing production scene API was measured separately through
`Frame` + `compose()`:

| Input entities | Placements |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 |
| 10 | 10 |
| 100 | 100 |
| 1,000 | 1,000 |

This is **scene placement cardinality**, not generic resolver cardinality.
The distinction is deliberate because there is currently no production path
connecting the two.

---

## 7. Retained memory

`tracemalloc` was used around real `Component` + `RuntimeGraph` + resolver +
cache objects.

Measured current allocations:

| Components | Resolved entries | Current Python bytes |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 19,029 |
| 10 | 10 | 224,031 |
| 100 | 32 | 1,489,870 |
| 1,000 | 32 | 9,259,997 |

Peak values were also recorded in the benchmark artifact.

These are Python engineering measurements, not a production allocator
certification. Because no production owner exists, no byte-budget policy was
added.

---

## 8. RuntimeGraph rebuild churn

Thirty local rebuilds were measured for each graph size:

| Components | Median rebuild |
|---:|---:|
| 32 | ~92,228 ns |
| 128 | ~362,885 ns |
| 512 | ~1,316,681 ns |

The values are local timing evidence and must not be interpreted as a
production frame budget.

---

## 9. Shared vs partitioned cache

Two independently constructed graphs with the **same semantic component IDs**
were resolved through one shared cache and then through two partitioned caches.

### Shared

```text
32 misses
32 hits
32 entries
```

### Partitioned

```text
64 misses
0 hits
64 entries
```

This demonstrates that shared caching can exploit exact fingerprint identity
across independent graph objects.

It does **not** justify a shared production cache because there is no production
multi-scene owner.

Conversely, no production LRU pollution was observed because no production
cache workload exists. Therefore no partitioning API is introduced.

---

## 10. Memory budget decision

No byte budget is introduced.

Reason:

```text
no production owner
        ↓
no production lifetime
        ↓
no production retained-memory budget
        ↓
byte-budget policy would be speculative
```

The existing bounded entry-count policy remains untouched.

---
